title: Live sampler splay and golden-trace harness
body:
Purpose:
This note describes the design, smoke-run scripts, and CI integration for a live-sampler splay plus golden-trace harness. Goal is to supplement existing profiling pipelines with a lightweight always-on sampler that captures representative short traces (3–30ms hotpath windows) and stores compact golden traces for deterministic regression detection across commits and infra changes.

Motivation and constraints:
- We need earlier detection of micro-regressions (alloc stalls, preemptions, kernel steals) that don’t show up in heavy-load benchmarks but affect p95/p99 on production-like bursts.
- The sampler must be safe to run on production-like nodes (no heavy overhead, <1% CPU, bounded memory per-sampler).
- Traces must be small, reproducible enough to diff, and annotated with workload fingerprints.
- CI gating must be fast: single-sample smoke should finish <90s for feedback, full golden comparison CI job can run in ~10–20m on dedicated runners.

Design overview:
1) Splayed sampling windows
   - Each node runs a lightweight agent (python wrapper around eBPF probes + perf record fallback).
   - Agent schedules short sampling windows with randomized splay to avoid synchronized probes: base interval = 30s, jitter = +-40% drawn from a seeded RNG (seed derived from node id + day) so samples are repeatable per-node/day for debugging.
   - When a sampling window triggers we capture: async stack traces (user + kernel), per-thread schedstat (runqueue wait, runtime), GPU allocator cross-check markers (when available), and a compact KV-cache hit/miss metric snapshot from the runtime diagnostics socket.

2) Golden traces and fingerprinting
   - A golden trace is a compact representation: timestamp, sampled stacks (top N frames), per-frame microtime deltas, k/v cache counters, and a workload fingerprint (token-length histogram, callsite hash, model-id).
   - We canonicalize frames by mapping addresses to function names + package path using local symbol cache. If symbols are missing fall back to module+offset.
   - Fingerprint: sha256 of stable attributes (model-id, prompt-size-bucket, top3-callsite-hashes) truncated to 12 chars for filenames.
   - Golden traces are stored in object storage under /goldens/{branch}/{fingerprint}/{date}/{node}.trace.gz. Naming convention used by CI to locate baselines.

3) Collector, uploader and retention policy
   - Collector component rotates local buffer (capped at 100MB) and uploads batched gzipped traces every 5 minutes to avoid too-frequent S3 PUTs.
   - Retention: keep 14 days of raw traces, 90 days of deduplicated goldens, and archive monthly snapshots for 1 year. Cost estimate: ~120KB per golden; expected 5k goldens/month ~600MB.

4) CI jobs and smoke harness
   - Smoke job (fast): runs a single-agent sampling run inside a small VM with the same runtime binary and a synthetic request pattern (short chat prompt bursts), collects 3 traces, computes quick similarity (edit distance on stack sequences + delta thresholds for additional metrics). Fails CI if similarity drops below 70% vs selected baseline or if new traces show >10% increase in average kernel preempt time. Target wall time < 90s.
   - Golden comparison job (full): triggered on merge to main + weekly nightlies. Runs the agent under a deterministic workload generator (seeded), collects 30 traces per node, collapses to top 5 fingerprints, and computes score against baseline goldens using: stack Jaccard, percentiles on alloc stalls, and delta of KV cache hit ratio. Produces a regression scorecard and annotated flamegraphs.

5) Flamegraph generation and artifact outputs
   - We provide a small toolkit (bash + python) to convert traces to folded stacks accepted by flamegraph.pl. The conversion normalizes timestamps into per-frame token-cost units to make cross-node flamegraphs comparable.
   - Artifacts emitted: folded.stacks.gz, aggregated-flame.svg, golden-diff.txt, regression-score.json (stringified numbers). CI stores artifacts to the run storage and links them in the PR.

6) Regression detection heuristics (initial ruleset)
   - Rule A (stack drift): If the average Jaccard similarity of top-10 frame sets across traces vs baseline < 0.65 => flag.
   - Rule B (alloc stalls): p95 alloc-stall delta > +15% => flag.
   - Rule C (kvcache): absolute drop in cache-hit ratio > 5 percentage points AND stack drift > 0.2 => high-priority fail.
   - Rule D (flake suppression): transient spikes (single-sample anomalies) require at least 3 of N samples to trigger to avoid flaky test failures. CI uses a 3-of-5 voting window.

7) Implementation notes and scripts
   - agent/collector: agent/collector/main.py (entrypoint for sampler, starts eBPF probes if permitted, otherwise falls back to perf record samples). Uses /var/run/serving-runtime/diag.sock to get runtime counters.
   - smoke-run.sh: minimal harness used by the quick CI job. Arguments: --duration 30 --seed 1234 --workload short-chat. Outputs: traces/*.trace.gz and quick.score.txt.
   - fold-and-emit.py: turns traces into folded stacks and produces aggregated flamegraph. Requires flamegraph.pl on PATH.

8) Safety and access controls
   - Agent must run with CAP_SYS_ADMIN only when eBPF mode is explicitly enabled via feature flag. Default runs in non-privileged perf fallback.
   - Uploaded traces are redacted: prompt payloads must not be captured; collectors only record callsite stacks and metrics. Any trace containing user prompt text is rejected and logged.

9) Troubleshooting checklist (oncall quick steps)
   - If no traces are uploaded: check collector logs /var/log/sampler.log, verify object-store credentials at /etc/sampler/s3.cfg, ensure uploader PID is alive.
   - If too many false positives in CI: increase jitter seed or widen Jaccard threshold; run local golden rebaseline with controlled workload to ensure baseline freshness.
   - If agent triggers high CPU: check number of concurrent sampler threads (default 1 per node), reduce sampling frequency, or switch to perf fallback mode.

10) Open questions / TODOs
   - Should we include GPU callstacks (cupti)? Current plan: optional module gated behind a vendor-driver capability check.
   - How to canonicalize function names across stripped prod binaries? Explore storing symbol servers or using addr2line mapping during CI artifact ingestion.
   - Integrate with trace-analytics UI in Console: prototype dashboard for golden-diff histograms and flamegraph overlays.

Appendix: quick smoke commands
- Run a single sample locally (non-privileged):
    sudo -E python3 agent/collector/main.py --mode perf --duration 10 --seed 9876 --workload short-chat --out traces/local.trace.gz

- Fold and view flamegraph (local):
    python3 fold-and-emit.py traces/local.trace.gz > folded.stacks
    ./flamegraph.pl folded.stacks > flame.svg

- Run CI-style quick scoring locally:
    ./smoke-run.sh --duration 30 --seed 42 --workload short-chat && cat quick.score.txt

Notes on uniqueness: this doc intentionally focuses on splayed always-on sampling and compact golden traces for quick CI gating rather than heavy continuous profilers or full-production deterministic reproducers. It is intended to complement existing profiling runbooks (profilers, flamegraph collectors) by offering a low-cost, high-signal pipeline that surfaces small regressions earlier in the commit cycle.
